title: Introduce RBAC bootstrapping CLI and rollback playbooks for Private installs
author: Claire Ng
release_notes: Add a small operatorless RBAC bootstrapping CLI for Private installs, idempotent Terraform module tweaks, and documented rollback playbooks for tenant bootstrap failures.
body:
Motivation: Private/on-prem installations sometimes run in environments where installing an operator is not allowed (air-gapped or locked-down clusters) or where the operator lifecycle is managed separately. Installer teams have asked for a minimal, auditable, operatorless path to seed tenant roles, cluster roles, and bootstrap service accounts, plus a clearly documented rollback playbook for failed bootstrap attempts. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI (rbac-bootstrap) and a set of rollback playbooks that can be used by SREs and install engineers, and also hardens Terraform modules for idempotency and safer retries. The aim is to reduce manual steps for tenant isolation while keeping a clear rollback surface.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New CLI: tooling/rbac-bootstrap/cli.py and a small shell wrapper for air-gapped invocation. The CLI accepts a tenant manifest (YAML), validates it, and applies RBAC objects in a deterministic order with built-in dry-run and checkpointing so partially-applied runs can resume.
- Rollback playbooks: docs/playbooks/rbac-bootstrap-rollback.md with explicit steps and a machine-readable rollback manifest that the CLI can ingest to revert partial state.
- Terraform module tweaks: modules/tenant-rbac/main.tf adjusted to export stable resource names and to tolerate create-if-not-exists flows used by the CLI; added tags and owner annotations for easier cleanup.
- E2E examples: examples/private-bootstrap/sample-tenant.yaml and a CI smoke harness that exercises a dry-run and simulated failure to validate rollback behavior.
- Tests: unit tests for cli validator and integration test stubs that run in CI (mock K8s server). The integration stubs are guarded so they don't run in ephemeral CI by default.

Design notes: The CLI intentionally does not require a cluster-level operator; it uses RBAC service account tokens and standard kubectl API operations. To make this safe for unattended runs, we added a checkpoint file (.rbac-bootstrap/checkpoints.json) written to a user-specified directory. Checkpoints include the exact resource fingerprints created so rollback can be precise. The rollback playbook documents both automated (CLI-driven) and manual rollback steps, covering:
- Reverting ClusterRoleBindings created in the bootstrap window
- Removing ServiceAccounts and their secrets
- Restoring tenant-specific namespace annotations if modified

Usage example (CLI): rbac-bootstrap --manifest sample-tenant.yaml --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig --checkpoint-dir /tmp/rbac-checks --dry-run
To perform an automated rollback: rbac-bootstrap rollback --checkpoint-dir /tmp/rbac-checks --confirm

Commits summary (high-level):
- Add initial CLI implementation and argument parser (cli.py)
- Add checkpointing and dry-run support
- Add rollback manifest reader and revert actions
- Terraform: make resource names stable; add ownership tags
- Docs: add playbook and example manifests
- Tests: unit tests for manifest validation and mock apply/revert

Files touched (high level):
- tooling/rbac-bootstrap/cli.py (+480 lines)
- tooling/rbac-bootstrap/README.md (+120 lines)
- docs/playbooks/rbac-bootstrap-rollback.md (+300 lines)
- modules/tenant-rbac/main.tf (+60 lines)
- examples/private-bootstrap/sample-tenant.yaml (+40 lines)
- tests/rbac/test_cli_validator.py (+70 lines)
- ci/bootsrap-smoke/harness.sh (+60 lines)
- charts/private-installer/templates/rbac-seed-job.yaml (+50 lines)

Review conversation snapshot (selected comments):
- Priya Shah: "Nice work on the checkpointing model — can we avoid writing secrets to disk in the checkpoint file? Suggest storing only resource UIDs and not secret contents." — Author (Claire): "Agreed. Checkpoint schema now only persists resource meta (kind, name, uid, timestamp) and the current code scrubs secret data before checkpointing. I added a unit test to assert no secret payloads are captured."
- Marcus Lee: "Terraform tweak looks good but please add a migration note; existing installs that relied on previous resource names could break during re-run." — Author: "Added migration section to the README and a safe flag `--skip-name-migration` to the CLI to preserve previous behavior for upgrades."
- Aaron Kim: "Is the rollback playbook idempotent? If a partial rollback fails, can operators re-run it safely?" — Author: "Yes — the CLI rollback verifies resource existence before attempting delete and records rollback steps to the checkpoint. The playbook documents re-run semantics and has guidance for when to call support."
- CI bot: "integration-stub skipped in default agents; unit tests passed on Python 3.10/3.11" — CI status: passed on final run.

CI and QA notes: CI initially failed on a linting step (black formatting) and on a flaky mock-test that assumed specific ordering for ClusterRoleBinding creation. Fixes:
- Formatting: applied black and added pre-commit hook in tooling/rbac-bootstrap/.pre-commit-config.yaml
- Flaky test: widened assertion to ignore ordering, added a retry loop for mock server registrations. Final CI run: all checks green (unit, lint, ci-smoke).

Operational considerations: The CLI is intended for use by on-prem install teams and will be included in the private-installer bundle as an alternative bootstrap path. It is not the primary path for hosted or managed clusters. The Terraform idempotency changes reduce chance of drift when operatorless CLI runs concurrently with Terraform apply; notes are included in the module README.

Backwards compatibility and release notes: This change is non-breaking for existing installs if they continue to use the operator path. For teams switching to the CLI, the README contains a migration checklist. The Terraform stable-name change could affect systems that hardcode resource names; a migration toggle `--skip-name-migration` is provided and included in the installer runbook.

Merge outcome: After approvals from Priya and Marcus and a green CI run, the PR was squash-merged to main on 2025-11-20. Changes are included in the private-installer v1.8 release notes and the RBAC tooling package.

Follow-ups: (1) Track ENG-1428 to add GCP/Azure-specific service account handling for private installer automation, (2) Add audit log integration so the bootstrap CLI can emit structured audit events to the console and optionally to a configured webhook, (3) Add a small K8s operator shim for environments that want a transition path from operatorless to operator-managed bootstrapping.
